children: First Advantage shares were lower after the company said it priced an underwritten secondary offering of 15 million shares at $21.80 a share.
The stock was 11% lower, at $21.03, in morning trade, but is still 60% higher in the past 12 months.

The software-and-data company said the shares were being sold by certain investment funds of Silver Lake Group and its affiliates. First Advantage isn't selling any shares and won't receive any proceeds from the sale of shares in the offering by the selling stockholder.
The offering is expected to close on or about Thursday.
